title: Update on N-central 2026.4 HF2 and ongoing security response
summary: We want to provide additional context on the N-central 2026.4 HF2 release, the protections it provides, and the additional work underway as part of our ongoing response. This hotfix addresses...
body_markdown:
We want to provide additional context on the N-central 2026.4 HF2 release, the protections it provides, and the additional work underway as part of our ongoing response. **This hotfix addresses critical security updates** and includes a number of security patches and technology updates that improve the overall security of N-central. Related CVEs have now also been published.


First and most importantly, customers running **on-premises N-central deployments should upgrade to HF2 as soon as possible and keep their servers inaccessible to the internet until the upgrade has been successfully completed.** **Hosted N-central servers have been upgraded by N-able and are back online.** All customers, both hosted and on-premises, must also **upgrade their Agents and Probes** . Download information:[N-central 2026.4 HF2 Release Notes | N-able Status](https://status.n-able.com/2026/11/10/n-central-2026-4-hf2-release-notes/)


## Setting the record straight


**Claims that N-able ignored responsible disclosure from the researcher are inaccurate.** The new vulnerabilities that the researcher published on November 9 were not responsibly disclosed through our established reporting channels. We maintain several reporting channels including an active bug bounty program specifically to enable security researchers to report potential vulnerabilities responsibly, and we work with researchers who use that process to investigate and address their findings.


## Why we’re taking a phased approach


Our priority has been to reduce customer risk as quickly as possible while ensuring each fix is safely developed and tested. Rather than keep customers offline until every identified issue could be addressed together, **we have prioritized these fixes based on the severity and exploitability of the vulnerabilities, addressing the highest-risk issues first, to help improve the overall security of your server.** All identified vulnerabilities that could be exploited via an unauthenticated user have been addressed. The remaining vulnerabilities require an authenticated N-central account often with elevated privileges, or additional conditions that limit exploitability, and will be addressed through subsequent hotfixes as we continue to prioritize the security and protection of our customers.


## What we’re seeing


We are observing scanning activity associated with the publicly released proof-of-concept code, but we have seen **no indications of compromise within N-central hosted servers** .


Confirming whether any individual customer environment has been compromised requires an assessment of that specific environment. Customers should apply the applicable hotfix and recommended security guidance, and our teams can work directly with customers who have concerns about their environments.


## Our continued focus


This work is not finished. A follow-up hotfix will provide further security updates, and our Security, Engineering, Operations, and Adlumin SecOps teams continue to actively monitor activity, assess the disclosed vulnerabilities, and implement necessary remediation.


**Protecting our partners and their customers remains our highest priority.** We recognize the disruption caused by the precautionary measures we have taken. We took those steps because we believe acting quickly to protect customer environments is the right thing to do, and we will continue providing updates and hands-on support as this work progresses.
